level_problem: B1 level: present continuous for an activity now; not C1.
B1/B2 stative-use contrast; the pair 001/002 is the real point, but each alone is easy.

other_correct: You are constantly changing your mind.
You're constantly changing your mind again.
instruction_problem: Answer given in the quote's content; 'complain' + two keywords makes it nearly a copy exercise. Simple-present version also correct (less targeted).
Gap before 'usually' invites 'do/don't ... drive' confusion; 'I do usually drive' is not sensible here, fine. Cue 'Don't phone me' makes the answer predictable.

answer: My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.
sense_problem: 'forever is borrowing' is a form few learners would write; 'forever' placement is the only issue, and it is a word-order slip rather than the tense point. Also 'forever' for annoyance is dated/less usual than 'always/constantly'.

answer: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
other_correct: when I'm speaking you're constantly interrupting me
you're interrupting me constantly when I'm speaking
when I'm speaking you're interrupting me constantly
I'm speaking when you're constantly interrupting me (odd but grammatical)
instruction_problem: No capitals or punctuation on cards, so several orders are open; the content is nearly given by the cards.

answer: This old suitcase is weighing nearly five kilos.

instruction_problem: 'Write to a customer' is superfluous. Cue (apologise) with 'for the delay' gives the verb; only the tense/form is tested. 'We are apologising' is less usual but correct; US 'apologize' correct.
level_problem: Fine for B2 formal register; C1 nuance is thin.

wrong_options_that_fit: Health minister has resigned over expenses (also used in news headlines, especially in British press; past simple too)
instruction_problem: 'Usual way' is vague; 'has resigned' and 'resigned' are also common in headlines.
sense_problem: Two options (resigns, has resigned) are real headline forms; 'usual' is arguable.
